examples.label: 科学 FR medium：温度与化学平衡

block.questionText:
The equilibrium system $N_2O_4(g) ightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)$ is endothermic in the forward direction. $NO_2$ is brown and $N_2O_4$ is colorless.
(a) Predict what happens to the color of the mixture when temperature increases.
(b) Use Le Chatelier's principle to explain the equilibrium shift.
(c) State one observation that would show a new equilibrium has been reached.

b.prompt: Explain the shift using Le Chatelier's principle.

c.prompt: State one sign of a new equilibrium.

block.correctAnswer: (a) The mixture becomes darker brown. (b) Increasing temperature favors the endothermic forward reaction, producing more $NO_2$. (c) A new equilibrium is reached when the color stops changing and remains constant.
block.solutionSteps: Part (a): The mixture becomes darker brown because the concentration of brown $NO_2$ increases.\nPart (b): By Le Chatelier's principle, adding heat favors the endothermic direction. Since the forward reaction is endothermic, the system shifts right, converting more $N_2O_4$ into $NO_2$.\nPart (c): One valid observation is that the color intensity stops changing over time, indicating the forward and reverse reaction rates have become equal again.
commonMistakes: Reversing the direction of the equilibrium shift when heat is added.
Describing equilibrium as a complete stop rather than equal forward and reverse rates.
Giving an observation that does not actually indicate the system has stabilized.
